maps.t: Entropy, Mapped — 3Blue1Brown on Compression
maps.d: Grant Sanderson's Compression is Intelligence series in twenty pages: surprise, prefix codes, entropy, cross-entropy and KL divergence, ending at the loss function every language model is trained on. Wordle and Hamming codes included, every claim timestamped into the video.

maps.t: Kun Chen, Mapped — Agent Tooling from First Principles
maps.d: The former L8 engineer's open-source shelf for working with coding agents: the ten AXI principles and his self-reported benchmark, the AXI CLIs, Lavish for reviewing HTML, the no-mistakes push gate, treehouse worktrees, backpass memory, gnhf and firstmate, the side builds, and the patterns across his repos. Eleven pages, quotes checked against the source.

maps.d: From the phone-addiction protocol and the three macronutrients of happiness to From Strength to Strength, Build the Life You Want, and the reverse bucket list. One page per idea.

maps.t: The Hierarchy of Money, Mapped
maps.d: Gregory Gundersen's village parable, turned into explainers. We start with the illustrated story — his wording, our animals — and grow a page for each idea: stones, bank money, reserves, reserve currency, fiat.

maps.t: The Man in the Arena, Mapped
maps.d: Roosevelt's Sorbonne speech of 1910, put back around its most-quoted paragraph: a clause-by-clause close reading, the whole address, the afterlife from Nixon to Brené Brown, the critiques, and the full text. Every quotation checked against the 1910 printing; the Mandela story checked and found wanting.

maps.d: Everything that runs on a cable, a rail, or a rack: gondolas, funiculars, cable cars, high-speed rail and maglev. How each works, how to spot it, where to ride the famous ones.

maps.t: Why We Invented Clowns
maps.d: Almost every human culture invented a clown. The licensed pressure valve, the near-universal lineage (jester, commedia, circus, sacred clown, trickster), the hospital-clown evidence, and the shadow.

maps.t: Where Did Your Job Title Come From?
